title_en: Peking University Founder Co., Ltd. and Beijing Honglou Research Institute v. Gaoshu Tianli Co., Ltd. and Gaoshu Co., Ltd. — dispute over computer software copyright infringement

full_text_en:
Peking University Founder Group Co., Ltd. and Beijing Honglou Computer Science and Technology Research Institute v. Beijing Gaoshu Tianli Technology Co., Ltd. and Beijing Gaoshu Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of computer software copyright

【Ruling Summary】

1. Pursuant to Article 67 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, a legal fact certified through notarization procedures shall be taken as the basis for finding facts by the People's Court, unless there is contrary evidence sufficient to overturn it. However, if the method of obtaining evidence itself is illegal, even if certified through notarization, the evidence so obtained cannot be used as the basis for finding facts.

2. Although the law provides numerous express provisions on illegal acts, due to the breadth of social life and the complexity of interests, the law more often adopts a non-exhaustive enumeration of illegal acts, but rather establishes legal principles, leaving the judge to make judgments based on interest balancing and value orientation.

3. Given that infringements of computer software copyright are highly concealed and difficult to investigate and obtain evidence, the infringed party's method of obtaining evidence through notarization is not improper in purpose, does not harm social public interests or the lawful rights and interests of others, and also facilitates solving the difficulty of obtaining evidence in such cases, helps deter and curb infringements, and helps strengthen the protection of intellectual property rights. Therefore, such a notarized evidence-gathering method should be deemed lawful and valid, and the evidence so obtained should also be used as the basis for finding the facts of the case.

4. If the alleged infringer of unauthorized installation and sale of pirated software cannot provide relevant evidence as to the source of the installed and sold software, it shall be presumed that it has infringed the copyright owner's right of reproduction and right of distribution.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2006) Min San Ti Zi No. 1

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Peking University Founder Group Co., Ltd. (formerly Beijing Peking University Founder Group Corporation), domiciled at No. 298 Chengfu Road, Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Wei Xin, Chairman.

Authorized Agent: Wang Lihua, attorney at Beijing Tianyuan Law Firm.

Authorized Agent: Li Qi, attorney at Beijing Tianyuan Law Firm.

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Beijing Honglou Computer Science and Technology Research Institute, domiciled at 2nd Floor, Founder Building, No. 9 Shangdi Fifth Street, Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Xiao Jianguo.

Authorized Agent: Wang Lihua, attorney at Beijing Tianyuan Law Firm.

Authorized Agent: Li Qi, attorney at Beijing Tianyuan Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Beijing Gaoshu Tianli Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 78 Suzhou Street, Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Li Wenping, General Manager.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Beijing Gaoshu Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 78 Suzhou Street, Haidian District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Li Wenping, General Manager.

The applicants for retrial, Peking University Founder Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Peking University Founder Company) and Beijing Honglou Computer Science and Technology Research Institute (hereinafter referred to as Honglou Research Institute), dissatisfied with the Civil Judgment (2002) Gao Min Zhong Zi No. 194 of the Beijing High People's Court and the Notice of Dismissal of Retrial Application (2003) Gao Min Jian Zi No. 196, applied to this Court for retrial in the case of dispute over computer software copyright infringement with Beijing Gaoshu Tianli Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gaoshu Tianli Company) and Beijing Gaoshu Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gaoshu Company). Upon review, this Court found that the application for retrial met the conditions for filing a retrial under Article 179, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and on March 7, 2006, decided to retry the case by civil ruling (2002) Min San Jian Zi No. 30-2. This Court formed a collegial panel composed of Kong Xiangjun, Deputy Chief Judge of the Third Civil Division, as presiding judge, trial judge Yu Xiaobai, and acting trial judge Xia Junli, and held a public hearing of this case. The court clerk Bao Shuo served as the court recorder. The authorized agent Li Qi of the applicants for retrial, Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute, and the legal representative Li Wenping of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. This case is now closed.

The first-instance court found that Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute were the copyright owners of the Founder Century RIP Software (hereinafter referred to as Founder RIP Software), Peking University Founder PostScript Chinese Font Library (hereinafter referred to as Founder Font Library), and Founder Wenhe Software V1.1 (hereinafter referred to as Founder Wenhe Software). Founder RIP Software and Founder Font Library Software were sold together as a bundle, collectively referred to as Founder RIP Software. The above software was installed on independent computers, and when connected to a laser imagesetter, it could realize the functions of the software.

Peking University Founder Company was a distributor in China of laser imagesetters produced by Screen (Hong Kong) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Screen Company). Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company had previously acted as agents for Peking University Founder Company in selling laser imagesetters, and the laser imagesetters they sold used Founder RIP Software and Founder Wenhe Software. In May 1999, due to a disagreement between the parties, the agency relationship was terminated. On April 17, 2000, Gaoshu Company entered into an agreement with Screen Company for the sale of laser imagesetters, stipulating that when Gaoshu Company sold KATANA-5055 laser imagesetters, it must be equipped with either Screen Company's genuine RIP software or Peking University Founder Company's genuine RIP software. If equipped with Founder RIP software, Gaoshu Company must order genuine Founder RIP software from Peking University Founder Company through Screen Company.

On July 20, 2001, an employee of Peking University Founder Company, in a personal capacity (using a pseudonym), entered into an "Electronic Publishing System Order Contract" with Gaoshu Tianli Company. The contracted supply was one KATANA FT-5055A laser imagesetter (without RIP), with a unit price of RMB 415,000. After the contract was signed, Peking University Founder Company paid Gaoshu Tianli Company a total of RMB 394,250 on July 20, 2001 and August 23, 2001, with an outstanding balance of RMB 20,750. Gaoshu Company issued receipts to the employee of Peking University Founder Company for the above payments on July 23, 2001 and August 23, 2001, respectively.

On August 22, 2001, an employee of Gaoshu Tianli Company installed a laser imagesetter in a room temporarily rented by an employee of Peking University Founder Company at Room 503, Building 84, Yongle Residential Area, Shijingshan District, Beijing, and installed pirated copies of Founder RIP Software and Founder Wenhe Software on two computers provided by Peking University Founder Company, and also provided a compact disc containing the above software burned onto it. Peking University Founder Company paid rent of RMB 3,000.

At the request of Peking University Founder Company, the Beijing National Trust Notary Public Office, on July 16, July 20, July 23, and August 22, 2001, in Room 503, Building 84, Yongle Residential Area, Shijingshan District, Beijing, and in Room 120, North Building, No. 6 Huayuan Road, Haidian District, Beijing, and Room 418, South Building (Beijing Houlang Shikong Graphic Technology Co., Ltd., formerly Beijing Zhongtang Color Printing Center, hereinafter referred to as "Houlang Company"), carried out on-site notarization of the process in which an employee of Peking University Founder Company, acting as an ordinary consumer, contacted Gaoshu Tianli Company to purchase KATANA FT-5055A laser imagesetter equipment, and Gaoshu Tianli Company installed Founder RIP Software and Founder Wenhe Software on the computers provided by Peking University Founder Company for use with the laser imagesetter. The notary office also conducted notarized preservation of evidence of the two computers provided by Peking University Founder Company and the pirated software installed on them, and produced five notarial records. Peking University Founder Company paid notarization fees of RMB 10,000.

On September 3, 2001, Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute filed a lawsuit with the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, alleging that Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company had illegally reproduced, installed, and sold the software, infringing their computer software copyright. They sought a judgment ordering Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company to: 1. cease the infringement, eliminate the effects, and make a public apology; 2. compensate economic losses of RMB 3,000,000; and 3. bear the litigation costs, preservation fees, evidence-gathering fees, and audit fees.

On September 24, 2001, the first-instance court, upon the application of Peking University Founder Company, conducted preservation of evidence of the financial account books, sales invoices, receipts, and order contracts of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company from January 1999 to September 2001. At the same time, it carried out property preservation of the bank deposits of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company, freezing RMB 97,454.23 in the account of Gaoshu Company at the Haidian Sub-branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Beijing Branch, and RMB 460,292.70 in the account of Gaoshu Tianli Company at the Haidian Sub-branch of the Haidian Branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Beijing Branch. Peking University Founder Company paid property and evidence preservation fees of RMB 15,520.

On September 28, 2001, the first-instance court commissioned Beijing Tianzhenghua Certified Public Accountants to audit the turnover and profits of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company from the sale of laser imagesetters and related equipment, as well as pirated Founder RIP Software and Founder Wenhe Software, from January 1999 to September 2001. On November 12, 2001, Beijing Tianzhenghua Certified Public Accountants issued a special audit report, stating that Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company had sold 82 sets of laser imagesetters in total during the above period, and that the laser imagesetters sold included single-unit sales as well as sales together with RIP software, film processors, or scanners. In addition, Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company also separately sold 13 sets of RIP software with unidentified brands. Peking University Founder Company paid audit fees of RMB 60,000.

On November 29, 2001, under the presiding of the first-instance court, the parties participated in an inspection of the two computers provided by Peking University Founder Company and the related software that had been preserved as notarized evidence. The inspection results showed that pirated Founder Wenhe Software was installed on the preserved computers, and the preserved software included pirated Founder RIP Software and Founder Wenhe Software. Both parties did not object to the inspection results. The normal market selling prices of Founder RIP Software and Founder Wenhe Software were RMB 100,000 and RMB 30,000, respectively.

The first-instance court held that: 1. In order to obtain evidence of infringement by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company, Peking University Founder Company invested considerable costs, including purchasing a laser imagesetter and renting a house, and adopted a "trap-gathering" method of evidence collection. This method was not prohibited by law and should be recognized. The notarial certificates also proved the process of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company installing pirated Founder software, and preserved evidence of the computers and pirated software on which pirated Founder software had been installed. The above notarial process and the content of the notarial preservation had been confirmed by the court, and Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company did not provide sufficient contrary evidence to overturn the content of the notarial certificates. 2. As sellers of computer equipment and related software, Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company had a duty of care regarding the copyright of others' computer software, and it was their obligation to refuse pirated software; otherwise, they should bear corresponding legal liability. The employees of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company in this case engaged in work that was an act performed in the course of their duties, and the party performing the contract was Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company. Therefore, Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company should bear corresponding legal liability. 3. Based on the existing evidence, it could not be determined that Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company had engaged in large-scale illegal production and sale of the above software nationwide. The Founder RIP and Founder Wenhe software of Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute had a long development cycle and significant investment. Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company had infringed the computer software copyright of Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute and should bear corresponding legal liability. Given that the actual quantity of pirated software sold by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company and the profits obtained were difficult to ascertain, the amount of compensation would be determined by the court comprehensively based on factors such as the development cost and market selling price of the software of Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute, and the subjective fault of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company in committing the infringement. The costs incurred by Peking University Founder Company for investigation and evidence-gathering, including the purchase price of the laser imagesetter, rent, and notarization fees, were necessary for the investigation and evidence-gathering in this case; therefore, the above expenses should be borne by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company. Given that the laser imagesetter could only work when connected to a computer host, and the laser imagesetter was not a direct carrier of the pirated software, while the computer hosts on which the pirated software was installed were provided by Peking University Founder Company, it was appropriate that Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company return the purchase price of the laser imagesetter to Peking University Founder Company, and Peking University Founder Company return the laser imagesetter to Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company. The audit fees, evidence and property preservation fees paid by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute in this case should also be borne by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company.

On December 20, 2001, the first-instance court rendered its judgment: 1. Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company shall immediately cease their infringement of reproducing and selling Founder RIP Software and Founder Wenhe Software; 2. Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company shall, within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, publish a notice in "Computer World" apologizing to Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute; 3. Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company shall jointly compensate Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute for economic losses in the amount of RMB 600,000; 4. Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company shall jointly reimburse Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute for the investigation and evidence-gathering expenses paid in this case (purchase price of the laser imagesetter RMB 394,250, rent RMB 3,000, notarization fees RMB 10,000) totaling RMB 407,250; 5. After Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company return the purchase price of the laser imagesetter of RMB 394,250, Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute shall return the laser imagesetter to Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company; 6. The other claims of Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute are dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 11,010, property preservation fee of RMB 15,520, and audit fee of RMB 60,000 shall all be jointly borne by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company.

Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Beijing High People's Court. Their grounds for appeal were: the first-instance court had found that Peking University Founder Company had disguised its identity, fabricated lies, and induced employees of Gaoshu Tianli Company to replace the genuine software originally bundled with the laser imagesetter with pirated Founder software, but did not make a finding on this; Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company had no other acts of reproducing or selling pirated Founder software other than the one set of pirated Founder software that was installed as a result of inducement and entrapment, but the first-instance court concluded that the quantity of Founder software installed by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company was difficult to ascertain; the notary public did not identify themselves, did not make on-site records, the facts recorded were incomplete, and the notarization was of illegal facts, so the notarial certificates were not lawful; the method used by Peking University Founder Company was illegal, and the first-instance court's recognition of this method as "trap-gathering" and its support thereof was erroneous; Founder Wenhe Software had no direct or indirect relationship with the laser imagesetter, nor was Founder RIP Software an inevitable choice for the laser imagesetter. The first-instance judgment lacked factual and legal basis and was unjust. The appellants requested that the first-instance judgment be set aside and that the litigation costs be borne by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute.

Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute submitted to the first-instance judgment.

The second-instance court confirmed most of the facts found by the first-instance court. It also found the following additional facts: According to the on-site notarial records made by the Beijing National Trust Notary Public Office in July and August 2001, an employee of Peking University Founder Company, using a pseudonym, contacted Gaoshu Tianli Company to purchase a laser imagesetter, actively proposed to buy pirated Founder RIP Software and Founder Wenhe Software, and an employee of Gaoshu Tianli Company stated that this could not be written into the contract but promised to sell the pirated software to Peking University Founder Company.

The second-instance court held: With regard to the notarial certificates issued by the Beijing National Trust Notary Public Office, Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company did not provide sufficient contrary evidence to overturn the content recorded in the notarial certificates, so the notarial certificates were lawful and valid civil evidence, and the content recorded therein was recognized. However, taken together with other evidence in this case, regarding the process of Peking University Founder Company purchasing the laser imagesetter over the course of a month, the notarial records only recorded five scenes, and the recording of the entire purchase process lacked continuity and completeness. Before obtaining other evidence that could prove that Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company had infringed its software copyright, Peking University Founder Company sent its employees to rent a private house, purchased the laser imagesetter sold by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company as an agent under a pseudonym, and actively proposed to buy pirated Founder software. From this, it can be seen that Peking University Founder Company's purchase of the laser imagesetter was a pretense, and its true intent was to obtain evidence of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company's sale of pirated Founder software. This method of evidence-gathering by Peking University Founder Company was not the only way to obtain evidence of infringement by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company, and such a method of evidence-gathering was contrary to the principle of fairness. If widely used, it would disrupt normal market order. Therefore, this method of evidence-gathering was not recognized. Given that Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company did not deny that they had sold pirated Founder software in this case, and the record of this fact in the notarial certificates was corroborated, the fact that Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company sold one set of pirated Founder RIP Software and Founder Wenhe Software in this case could be confirmed. The first-instance court's conclusion that the quantity of pirated software sold by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company was difficult to ascertain, and its consequent determination of the amount of compensation payable by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company on a discretionary basis, was erroneous. Given that the evidence-gathering method of Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute was not recognized, and the fact that Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company sold only one set of the pirated software involved in this case, the investigation and evidence-gathering expenses incurred by Peking University Founder Company for this case, including the purchase price of the laser imagesetter, rent, and audit fees, should be borne by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute themselves; the notarization fees, evidence and property preservation fees should be borne by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company. The first-instance court's findings of fact were unclear, but its application of law was correct. The appeal requests of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company were partially reasonable, and the reasonable part was supported.

On July 15, 2002, the second-instance court rendered its judgment: 1. Items (1), (2), and (6) of the first-instance judgment were affirmed; 2. Items (3), (4), and (5) of the first-instance judgment were reversed; 3. Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company shall jointly compensate Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute for economic losses in the amount of RMB 130,000; 4. Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company shall jointly reimburse Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute for the notarization fees paid in this case in the amount of RMB 10,000. The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 11,010 shall be borne jointly by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company in the amount of RMB 2,386, and jointly by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute in the amount of RMB 8,624; the second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 11,010 shall be borne jointly by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company in the amount of RMB 2,386, and jointly by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute in the amount of RMB 8,624.

Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute, dissatisfied with the second-instance judgment, filed a retrial application with the second-instance court. The Beijing High People's Court, upon review, rejected the retrial application of Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute on August 20, 2003.

Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute, dissatisfied with the second-instance judgment of the Beijing High People's Court and the notice rejecting the retrial application, filed a petition for retrial with this Court. Their main reasons were: relevant evidence had already confirmed that the infringing acts of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company were multiple and large-scale, and the second-instance court's order for Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company to compensate Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute only RMB 130,000 for the loss of one set of genuine Founder software was erroneous. Both the first-instance and second-instance courts confirmed that the notarial certificate issued by Beijing Guoxin Notary Public Office was lawful and valid. From the several on-site records attached to that notarial certificate, it could be seen that the pirated Founder software sold by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company was by no means limited to the one set sold to an employee of Peking University Founder Company. The second-instance court's amended decision requiring Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute to bear the costs of investigation and evidence collection was erroneous. The evidence collection method adopted by Peking University Founder Company did not violate any prohibitive provisions of laws or regulations. Without adopting such an evidence collection method, not only would it be impossible to obtain direct and effective evidence, but it would also be impossible to discover other clues of infringing acts by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company. Peking University Founder Company did not have any issue of violating fairness or disrupting market order; it did not purchase a large number of laser imagesetters to increase the amount of compensation. The purpose of Peking University Founder Company's investigation, evidence collection, and filing of the lawsuit was to combat piracy and protect its own legitimate rights and interests. The second-instance court's erroneous determination of facts and application of law failed to serve the purpose of correcting infringing acts, and effectively created difficulties and obstacles for copyright holders to protect their legitimate rights and interests, which was detrimental to the protection of intellectual property.

Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company argued in their defense that the notarial certificate issued by Beijing Guoxin Notary Public Office was completed under circumstances where the notary knew that the employee of Peking University Founder Company was pretending to be a buyer, intending to use deceptive means to obtain evidence of their company's "infringement." Moreover, the content of the record was incomplete and was not the result of an on-site supervision record; a record made solely based on the notary's subjective memory was not objective, lacked impartiality, and greatly differed from the information known to their company. The "trap evidence collection" method adopted by Peking University Founder Company was a destruction of legal order, social morality, and normal commercial order. Peking University Founder Company fabricated reasons and repeatedly requested their company's employees to install a set of pirated Founder software for them. This deceptive practice was "entrapment" and violated public order and good customs.

This Court finds that the facts determined by the first-instance court are basically true, but the second-instance court's determination that Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company only sold one set of pirated Founder RIP software and Founder Wenhe software is erroneous.

Additionally, it is found: The five on-site records attached to the notarial certificate submitted by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute prove the following facts: 1. The "On-site Record (II)" dated July 6, 2001, records that an employee of Gaoshu Tianli Company stated: "We have sold quite a few of these, compatible ones, no problem, exactly the same as the genuine version. Look, this one is actually a compatible RIP." 2. The "On-site Record (III)" dated July 20, 2001, records that an employee of Gaoshu Tianli Company stated: during the same period, they sold a laser imagesetter to "Houlang Company," using "compatible" software; and made the same sale to "Baoleiyuan" (Beijing Baoleiyuan Technology Development Co., Ltd., hereinafter referred to as Baoleiyuan Company). 3. The "On-site Record (IV)" dated July 23, 2001, records that employees of Peking University Founder Company and the notary observed the installation and commissioning of a laser imagesetter by an employee of Gaoshu Tianli Company for Houlang Company. According to the statement of the Gaoshu Tianli Company employee, the laser imagesetter was also installed with Founder RIP software, which was also "compatible." Subsequently, the Gaoshu Tianli Company employee provided the Peking University Founder Company employee with a list of customers who had purchased the same laser imagesetter, which recorded the names, contact numbers, and contacts of customers including "Baoleiyuan Production Center" (i.e., Baoleiyuan Company), "Rainbow Printing," "Shangpin," "Zhongtang (Tang) Color Printing" (i.e., Houlang Company), and "Bureau Printing Factory." 4. The "On-site Record (V)" dated August 22, 2001, records that Gaoshu Tianli Company sold another laser imagesetter identical to the one in this case to "Hailesi (phonetic)." Furthermore, according to this record, Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company sold laser imagesetters in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Langfang, Shanxi, Shenyang, and other places, "selling everywhere except Tibet and Qinghai," and regarding the software, "few buy the genuine version, only the startup disk is replaced, the rest is the same." For the above facts proven by the notarial certificate, Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company provided no evidence to refute them. Furthermore, the parties do not dispute that compatible software is pirated software.

After the second-instance judgment became effective, Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute, based on the clues of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company's customers who purchased and used pirated software as reflected in the above on-site records, reported the matter to the relevant administrative department for industry and commerce. In October 2002, during the investigation by the relevant administrative department for industry and commerce of entities including Houlang Company and Baoleiyuan Company, Peking University Founder Company commissioned notaries from Beijing Guoxin Notary Public Office to accompany them and conduct evidence preservation notarization of the software installed on the users' premises. During the investigation, Houlang Company provided the administrative department for industry and commerce with its contract for purchasing the laser imagesetter from Gaoshu Company and stated in writing that the pirated software it had installed was purchased from Gaoshu Company. In a separate lawsuit filed by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute against Baoleiyuan Company, the court's judgment confirmed that the pirated software installed by Baoleiyuan Company was purchased from Gaoshu Company. Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company failed to provide relevant evidence regarding the source of the pirated software they sold.

Additionally, it is found that the laser imagesetter purchased by Peking University Founder Company from Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company has been sold by an affiliate of Peking University Founder Company. During the trial of this Court, Peking University Founder Company indicated that it waives its claim for compensation for the expenditure on purchasing the said laser imagesetter. Beijing Peking University Founder Group Company has changed its name to Founder Group Co., Ltd., with its legal representative changed to Wei Xin. The legal representative of Honglou Research Institute has been changed to Xiao Jianguo.

Opinion of the Court: The parties to this case have no dispute that Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute jointly own the copyright in the Founder RIP software and the Founder Wenhe software. Both the first-instance and second-instance courts determined that the acts of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company constituted infringement of the copyright of Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute, but they differed in their determinations of the relevant evidence and case facts, as well as the determination of tort liability. Based on the first-instance and second-instance judgments and the reasons for the retrial application by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute, this case mainly involves disputed issues such as the legality of the evidence collection method adopted by Peking University Founder Company, the nature of the alleged infringing acts, and the determination of the amount of damages.

(1) Whether the evidence collection method involved in this case is lawful

According to Article 67 of the Civil Procedure Law, legal facts proved through notarization procedures shall be taken by the people's court as the basis for ascertaining facts, unless there is contrary evidence sufficient to overturn them. The installation of pirated Founder software by Gaoshu Tianli Company is a fact proved by notarization in this case. Since Gaoshu Company and Gaoshu Tianli Company have no contrary evidence sufficient to overturn it, the authenticity of this fact should be confirmed. The method by which the fact proved by notarization is obtained concerns whether the evidence collection method itself is illegal. If the evidence collection method adopted is itself illegal, even if it is proved by notarization, the evidence obtained cannot be used as the basis for ascertaining case facts. Because if illegal evidence were to gain legality due to being proved by notarization, that would not only be inconsistent with the notarial rule that a notary office must review the legality of the notarial matter, but also be detrimental to curbing illegal evidence collection and protecting the legitimate rights and interests of others. The second-instance court, while denying the legality of the evidence collection method of Peking University Founder Company, also relied on the legal facts obtained through that method, which were proved by notarization, as the basis for ascertaining case facts. This is improper.

In civil litigation, although the law provides many explicit provisions on illegal acts, due to the breadth of social relations and the complexity of interests, except where there are explicit provisions, the law does not adopt an exhaustive listing of illegal acts. Instead, there is more room for resolution based on balancing interests and value orientation. Therefore, for acts not explicitly prohibited by law, the judgment should mainly be based on the substantive legitimacy of the act. In this case, through the notarial evidence collection method, Peking University Founder Company not only obtained evidence of Gaoshu Tianli Company's on-site installation of pirated Founder software, but also obtained evidence and leads regarding its sales of pirated software to other customers and the commission of similar infringing acts. The purpose was not improper, and the act did not harm the public interest or the legitimate rights and interests of others. Additionally, given that computer software copyright infringement acts have characteristics such as high concealment and difficulty in evidence collection, adopting such an evidence collection method is beneficial for solving the difficulty of evidence collection in such cases, plays a role in deterring and curbing infringing acts, and also aligns with the legal spirit of strengthening intellectual property protection according to law. Furthermore, the evidence collection method adopted by Peking University Founder Company did not infringe upon the legitimate rights and interests of Gaoshu Company and Gaoshu Tianli Company. The reasons for the retrial application by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute are legitimate and should be supported.

Accordingly, the evidence collection method involved in this case is lawful and valid, and the facts proved by the evidence obtained should be used as the basis for deciding the case. The second-instance court's determination that "such an evidence collection method is not the only way to obtain evidence of infringement, and is contrary to the principle of fairness, and if widely used, will cause damage to normal market order" is improper.

(2) Regarding the characterization of the infringing acts in this case

The object of the lawsuit filed by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute is the infringing acts of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company in illegally copying, installing, and selling pirated software. Since Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company failed to provide relevant evidence regarding the source of the pirated software they sold, it should be presumed that their infringing acts included copying. That is, Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company infringed upon the reproduction rights and distribution rights of Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute in the Founder RIP software and Founder Wenhe software.

(3) Regarding the quantity of copied and sold pirated software and the amount of damages

According to the content proved by notarization, the employee of Gaoshu Tianli Company stated that, in addition to selling pirated software to Peking University Founder Company, they also sold "compatible" pirated software of the same type to customers such as Houlang Company and Baoleiyuan Company, and provided a "customer list." Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company provided no contrary evidence to refute this. Among these, the fact of selling the same type of pirated software to Houlang Company and Baoleiyuan Company was also corroborated by the rights enforcement actions of Peking University Founder Company after the second-instance judgment. Although the first-instance and second-instance courts did not conduct cross-examination on the facts in the audit report concerning Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company's sales of 82 sets of laser imagesetters and 13 separate sets of RIP software, the aforementioned facts are sufficient to prove that the quantity of pirated software sold by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company was not just one set. The first-instance court, finding it difficult to ascertain the actual quantity of pirated software copied and sold by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company and the profits obtained, and considering factors such as the development costs and market sales prices of Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute's software, as well as the subjective fault of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company in committing the infringing acts, exercised its discretion in accordance with the provisions of the Copyright Law then in effect to order Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company to compensate Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute for losses of RMB 600,000. This was not clearly inappropriate. The second-instance court's support for only RMB 130,000 in damages for one set of genuine software for Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute was without basis.

(4) Regarding how the relevant costs should be shared

The costs claimed by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute to be borne by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company include litigation fees, preservation fees, evidence collection fees, and audit fees. Among these, evidence collection fees include notarization fees, machine purchase costs, and rent. Regarding this request of Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute, the first-instance court's full support was not improper. Given that the involved laser imagesetter was sold by an affiliate of Peking University Founder Company after the second-instance judgment, and Peking University Founder Company has indicated that it waives its claim for compensation for this expenditure, this should be permitted.

In summary, the second-instance court's determination of some facts related to the infringing acts of Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company in this case was unclear, and the application of law was improper, which should be corrected. The main reasons for the retrial application by Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute are established, and this Court supports them. Pursuant to Article 46, Paragraph 1, Item (2) of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China before its revision in 2001 and Article 177, Paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment (2002) Gao Min Zhong Zi No. 194 of the Beijing High People's Court;

2. Affirm Items (1), (2), (3), and (6) of the Civil Judgment (2001) Yi Zhong Zhi Chu Zi No. 268 of the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, namely:
   (1) Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company shall immediately cease the infringing acts of copying and selling the Founder RIP software and Founder Wenhe software;
   (2) Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company shall, within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, publish a notice in "Computer World," publicly apologizing to Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute, with the costs borne by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company;
   (3) Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company shall jointly compensate Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute for economic losses in the amount of RMB 600,000;
   (6) Dismiss the other litigation claims of Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute;

3. Amend Item (4) of the Civil Judgment (2001) Yi Zhong Zhi Chu Zi No. 268 of the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court to: Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company shall jointly compensate Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute for the investigation and evidence collection costs incurred for this case (rent RMB 3,000, notarization fee RMB 10,000), totaling RMB 13,000;

4. Set aside Item (5) of the Civil Judgment (2001) Yi Zhong Zhi Chu Zi No. 268 of the Beijing No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, namely, that Peking University Founder Company and Honglou Research Institute, after receiving the return of the machine purchase price of RMB 394,250 from Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company, should return the laser imagesetter to Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company.

The first-instance and second-instance case acceptance fees totaling RMB 22,020, the property and evidence preservation fee of RMB 15,520, and the audit fee of RMB 60,000 shall be borne by Gaoshu Tianli Company and Gaoshu Company.

This judgment is final.
